known_base_failures.approval_note: Decision KAN-117 10631 (reviewer): entries 1-5 approved for the research-only paired ENGINEERING SMOKE protocol of axios-5892 only — explicit acceptance of unavailable coverage, not proof those behaviours are correct; 3-5: Node compatibility is a hypothesis, not an established cause. #6: option (c) isolated re-check, NOT an unconditional waiver; isolation-qualified/advisory, never a full-suite pass; does not establish order safety. Bound below to base, runtime and this exact set (sha256 over entries + isolation_rechecks); image ids are bound by freeze v2. Identities from runs 43760213045, 43761598428, 43762848617.

entries.justification: Environmental by design: the test makes a REAL request to postman-echo.com; the verification sandbox has no outbound network, so DNS fails (EAI_AGAIN). It cannot pass in this environment regardless of the code. Residual: query-parsing regressions against that live endpoint are not observable here.

Environmental by design: the test makes a REAL request to www.google.com and has no catch handler, so with no outbound network it never calls done() and Mocha times out. Residual: the HTTPS-agent assertion is not observable here.

Runtime incompatibility (likely, not reproduced on another Node): the test supplies a custom lookup that returns a single address; Node 24 (the agent image) calls lookup expecting the all-addresses form and throws ERR_INVALID_IP_ADDRESS before any request. Unrelated to the compression issue. Residual: custom-lookup regressions are not observable on this Node; only this exact code is excused, any other failure of this test is a regression.
As the previous entry (async lookup returning [address, family]): Node 24 lookup contract, ERR_INVALID_IP_ADDRESS before any request. Same residual and exact-code limit.
As the previous entries (async lookup returning only an IP string): Node 24 lookup contract, ERR_INVALID_IP_ADDRESS before any request. Same residual and exact-code limit.

isolation_rechecks.full_title: supports http with nodejs should support max content length
isolation_rechecks.justification: Fails in the full suite on base/empty/gold in every run but passes ALONE 3/3 on the base (run 43762848617): an in-suite interaction/order failure, cause not established. maxContentLength is enforced in the same response pipeline as decompression (this task), so it is NOT excepted: it is accepted only if its one isolated re-check on a fresh copy of the same candidate tree passes. Limitation: isolated success does not establish full-suite order safety and can miss interaction-only regressions.
